description: A tech lead must finalize an eight-week engineering investment plan for reducing checkout-platform technical debt, choosing the work allocation, sequencing, and follow-up commitments after the normal planning review.

shared_context.S1: The checkout platform has an eight-week engineering investment cycle starting next Monday.
shared_context.S2: The current draft plan includes database-schema cleanup, contract-test maintenance, dependency maintenance, and removal of unused staging infrastructure, but it does not assign final effort or sequence.
shared_context.S3: The team has seven engineer-weeks available for these four work items during the cycle, with one additional engineer-week available for unplanned follow-up.
shared_context.S4: Maya owns the final investment-plan decision.
shared_context.S5: The team's normal planning review asks the backend, QA, security, and cloud-cost owners to report any concrete constraints before the plan is finalized.
shared_context.S6: The dependency-maintenance item has no separate engineer-week estimate in the planning template; for this review, recording its required deadline and sequencing it within the plan are sufficient, and no additional sizing estimate is required for finalization.

PF1.text: While fixing an unrelated checkout query yesterday, Ethan confirmed that the schema cleanup requires exactly 3 engineer-weeks because an undocumented table-lock workaround must be replaced before the cleanup can be considered complete; he has not updated the planning document yet.

PF2.text: Lina measured the contract-test maintenance this morning and confirmed that stabilizing the flaky suite requires exactly 2 engineer-weeks, including a deterministic test fixture; she recorded the measurement in her QA notes but has not posted it to the planning channel.

PF3.text: During a dependency review for another service today, Owen confirmed that the checkout service's current payment-library version reaches end of vendor support at the end of week 2, so the dependency update must be completed by the end of week 2 and tracked as a security-maintenance commitment; he has not filed the finding yet.

PF4.text: Grace found while reconciling the cloud bill that an unused staging environment costs exactly $18,000 per month and can be removed in exactly 1 engineer-week; because the next billing period begins Monday, the cleanup should be the first work item, but she has not added the anomaly to the investment proposal.

acceptance_conditions: The schema cleanup must receive exactly 3 engineer-weeks.
Contract-test stabilization must receive exactly 2 engineer-weeks.
The dependency update must be completed by the end of week 2.
Staging infrastructure cleanup must receive exactly 1 engineer-week.
The staging cleanup priority must contain the word first.
The plan order must begin with staging cleanup and include schema cleanup, contract-test stabilization, and dependency update.
A security-maintenance commitment for the dependency update must exist and cite PF3.
A commitment mentioning staging cost and cleanup must exist and cite PF4.
The plan must reserve exactly one additional engineer-week for unplanned follow-up.
The schema-lock workaround must be cited in the justification.

content_checks.C5: 'first' in decisions['staging_cleanup_priority'] or 'First' in decisions['staging_cleanup_priority'] or 'FIRST' in decisions['staging_cleanup_priority']
content_checks.C6: any('PF3' in c.get('fact_ids', []) and ('security' in c['detail'] or 'maintenance' in c['detail'] or 'security' in c['type'] or 'maintenance' in c['type'] or 'deadline' in c['type']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: len(decisions['plan_order']) == 4 and decisions['plan_order'][0] in ['staging cleanup', 'staging_cleanup', 'staging infrastructure removal', 'staging_infrastructure_removal', 'removal of unused staging infrastructure'] and any('staging' in c for c in decisions['plan_order']) and any('schema' in c for c in decisions['plan_order']) and any('contract' in c for c in decisions['plan_order']) and any('dependency' in c for c in decisions['plan_order'])
content_checks.C12: any('PF4' in c.get('fact_ids', []) and '18,000' in c['detail'] and ('cleanup' in c['detail'] or 'staging' in c['detail'] or 'removal' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The schema cleanup allocation changes from an unspecified generic effort to exactly 3 engineer-weeks, and the schema-lock workaround becomes the required cited justification.
The contract-test allocation changes from unspecified maintenance effort to exactly 2 engineer-weeks.
The dependency update changes from ordinary maintenance to a completion deadline at the end of week 2 and requires a security- or maintenance-referenced commitment citing PF3.
The staging cleanup changes to exactly 1 engineer-week, moves to first priority because of the exact $18,000 monthly cost, and requires a commitment linking that cost to cleanup while citing PF4.
